message:
Here is a deck to revise routing and switching facts with.

{"title":"Routing and switching","cards":[{"front":"What does ARP resolve?","back":"An IPv4 address to a MAC address on the local segment."},{"front":"Default administrative distance of OSPF?","back":"110."},{"front":"Default administrative distance of eBGP?","back":"20."},{"front":"Which VLAN carries untagged frames on an 802.1Q trunk?","back":"The native VLAN (VLAN 1 unless changed)."},{"front":"What does STP's root bridge election compare?","back":"The bridge ID: priority first, then the MAC address."},{"front":"Which port does SSH use?","back":"TCP 22."},{"front":"Name the common OSPF LSA types and what each one describes.","back":"Type 1 router LSAs describe each router's own links inside one area. Type 2 network LSAs are sent by the designated router for a broadcast segment and list the routers attached to it. Type 3 summary LSAs carry inter-area prefixes from an area border router. Type 4 summary LSAs tell other areas how to reach an autonomous system boundary router. Type 5 external LSAs carry routes redistributed into OSPF and flood through the whole domain except stub areas. Type 7 NSSA external LSAs carry external routes inside a not-so-stubby area until the border router turns them into type 5. Type 1 router LSAs describe each router's own links inside one area. Type 3 summary LSAs carry inter-area prefixes from an area border."},{"front":"What is the usable host count of a /30?","back":"Two."},{"front":"What does a /31 give you on a point-to-point link?","back":"Two usable addresses (RFC 3021), with no network or broadcast address."},{"front":"Which protocol synchronises clocks?","back":"NTP, on UDP 123."},{"front":"What does DHCP snooping protect against?","back":"Rogue DHCP servers handing out addresses on access ports."},{"front":"What is a stateful firewall's state table?","back":"Its record of open connections, used to allow matching return traffic."},{"front":"What does PAT translate?","back":"Many inside addresses to one outside address, told apart by port."},{"front":"Which command shows the routing table on IOS?","back":"show ip route"},{"front":"What does err-disabled mean on a switchport?","back":"The switch shut the port after a violation, such as port security or BPDU guard."},{"front":"Which multicast address do OSPF routers use for all SPF routers?","back":"224.0.0.5."},{"front":"What does LACP negotiate?","back":"An EtherChannel bundle between two devices (IEEE 802.3ad)."},{"front":"What is the purpose of a VRF?","back":"Separate routing tables on one router, so address spaces can overlap."},{"front":"Which record maps a name to an IPv6 address?","back":"AAAA."},{"front":"What does traceroute rely on?","back":"TTL expiry: each hop sends back ICMP Time Exceeded."}]}
